newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania and Hungary sign historic treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania and Hungary sign historic treaty.

text.p: Romania and Hungary signed a key treaty on Monday to end centuries-old disputes and to boost the two ex-communist countries' chances of joining NATO and the European Union.

The prime ministers of Romania and Hungary, Nicolae Vacaroiu and Gyula Horn, signed the pact in the western city of Timisoara, on the border with Yugoslavia and Hungary, in the presence of Romania's President Ion Iliescu.
"We have witnessed a special event, with deep impact on Romanian-Hungarian relations, and with a European and international impact," Vacaroiu said after signing the document with Horn.
The signing ceremony took place in the local government office in central Timisoara, ringed by a tight security cordon.
The treaty caps five years of negotiations. It stipulates inviolability of borders and guarantees the rights of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians.
